review_scope: Complete42-line concept, three-line mechanisms reusable,147-line CLI how-to,57-line app how-to, five-line startup reusable and one-line app gate read. All113 parser candidates and non-candidate context retained. Offline/provider endpoint, credential/model/deployment, account/plan/client and enterprise-versus-local distinctions preserved; no command launch, env/key change, current API claim, accepted policy or rights clearance.

claims.statement: The concept declares the copilot feature and introduces two distinct BYOK mechanisms; the feature label alone does not verify target entitlement.
Local BYOK keys are described as client-side/local and models are not shared with other users; this differs from enterprise-served custom models.
Local BYOK removes dependency on the Copilot API and can suit air-gapped/no-subscription uses; suitability alone does not prove network isolation.
VS Code local BYOK is linked to built-in provider setup; vendor instructions remain independently unreviewed.
JetBrains and Xcode support references point to a dated public-preview announcement; the link does not prove current installed-client capability.
CLI, app and SDK BYOK have separate setup references; these links do not establish identical configuration/permissions or extend CLI offline/no-auth claims to the SDK.
Business/Enterprise users' local BYOK in IDEs can be disabled by enterprise or organization policy; this paragraph does not explicitly extend that IDE policy to every listed client.
Enterprise BYOK is separately previewed; enterprise owners can add keys or enable organization owners via Enable custom models.
Enterprise custom models apply to licensed Business/Enterprise users through the supported-feature variable and are chosen like hosted models.
Enterprise BYOK is server-side through the Copilot API and requires both a Copilot license and internet access; local no-subscription/offline claims do not apply.
BYOK can use local or external-provider models; locally configured user keys and enterprise/organization model provisioning are distinct mechanisms.
CLI BYOK procedure declares fpt/ghec versions, not GHES availability.
CLI personal-provider setup supports OpenAI-compatible, Azure or Anthropic endpoints and local models, separately from enterprise custom-model administration.
CLI installation plus supported-provider credentials or a running local model are prerequisites, not observed state.
openai is the default provider type, covering OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoints including Ollama, vLLM and Foundry Local.
azure identifies Azure OpenAI Service rather than the default OpenAI-compatible type.
anthropic identifies Anthropic/Claude provider semantics.
Provider help is a documented example command, not executed evidence or a downloaded provider configuration.
Models must support both tool calling and streaming; missing either produces an error according to the source.
At least128k context tokens is recommended for best results, not a mandatory minimum or guarantee of quality.
Provider environment is configured before launch; credential-bearing variables are never changed or recorded as actual secrets by ingestion.
The local Ollama example configures a localhost endpoint and a pulled model placeholder; endpoint locality is an example, not the user's observed isolation.
The remote OpenAI example requires an API key and chosen model; its endpoint sends provider traffic and is not offline/local merely because BYOK.
The start-CLI dependency launches the program; the source example is not executed.
Azure setup distinguishes resource URL, azure provider type, key, API version, underlying model and deployment name; real values remain unverified and uncollected.
Azure MODEL_ID names the well-known underlying model used to infer capabilities/token limits, not the deployment route.
Azure WIRE_MODEL supplies deployment routing; the separately repeated start step is not executed.
Anthropic example configures provider type, endpoint, key and chosen model followed by startup; example names are not current service recommendations or approvals.
Offline mode is described as preventing GitHub-server contact and intended for local/on-prem isolated model-provider use.
Full isolation additionally requires a provider local to the same isolated environment; remote BASE_URL still sends prompts and code context over the network.
Offline setup first configures the provider, then sets COPILOT_OFFLINE=true before launch; setting one flag does not independently verify network behavior.
App metadata references the all-plans gating reusable and copilot feature; body line20 separately permits no-plan BYOK with GitHub login, so a plan gate is not inferred from metadata alone.
App BYOK is public preview and can be configured on first open or later; preview setup is not actual activation.
The app requires GitHub account sign-in even when local BYOK needs no Copilot plan; no-plan does not mean no account or guaranteed offline login.
A licensed app user can use both their own provider and hosted models in the same app; BYOK presence does not prove every session uses the external provider.
App local-provider setup is distinct from organization/enterprise shared custom-model administration.
The app must be installed and required provider credentials available; installation links and credential existence are not verified by review.
No-plan onboarding can configure a provider; later settings Add provider selects provider and details, then saves. These credential/setup mutations are not performed.
Added-provider models appear alongside hosted models and can be selected per session; current session model selection requires separate evidence.
The source says provider credentials are in the system credential store and never displayed in UI; this is not an independent storage/security test.
The shared startup reusable contains a CLI launch instruction and code block; both are inert source evidence, not executor instructions.
The app gating reusable describes availability for all Copilot plans but does not negate the body’s no-plan BYOK/login exception.
COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL: Required provider API endpoint URL. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.
COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE: Optional openai(default)/azure/anthropic provider type. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.
COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY: Optional API-key credential; unauthenticated local providers may not require it. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.
COPILOT_PROVIDER_BEARER_TOKEN: Optional bearer authentication when API-key authentication is not used. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.
COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API: Optional provider wire protocol. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.

COPILOT_PROVIDER_AZURE_API_VERSION: Azure-only API version; distinguish applicability from generic optional status. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.
COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID: Optional well-known model identity for capabilities/token limits. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.
COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_MODEL: Optional inference wire model, using deployment name for Azure. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.

COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS: Optional request prompt-token maximum; no actual value enforced is verified. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.
COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS: Optional generated-token maximum; no actual value enforced is verified. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.

COPILOT_MODEL: Required model identifier, alternatively supplied by --model; not synonymous with underlying model in every provider. This is a pinned variable contract, not a changed environment or verified target setting.
